newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Plane smashes into Sao Paulo homes, 103 dead.
newsitem.headline: Plane smashes into Sao Paulo homes, 103 dead.

text.p: A Fokker-100 aircraft from Brazil's TAM airline slammed into homes in a densely populated area of Sao Paulo on Thursday, killing all 95 on board and eight people on the ground, authorities said.
Rio de Janeiro-bound Flight 402 caught fire as it skidded over the rooftops of the middle-class neighbourhood of Parque Jabaquara, where it tore through stores and homes before coming to a stop.

The plane barrelled through the neighbourhood as residents were on their way to work, leaving a fiery trail of destruction. One eyewitness said jet fuel fell from the sky seconds before the crash, drenching a man on the ground who died after becoming engulfed in flames.
Wreckage of the plane was strewn amid three blocks of homes. Military police said at least eight people were killed on the ground.

A spokesman at Sao Paulo's Congonhas regional airport said all 89 passengers and six crew members were confirmed dead. Firemen were removing bodies from the crash site and lining them up in black plastic bags on a nearby sidewalk.

TAM said the plane was carrying more than a dozen executives of Brazilian and international firms. They included American David Francis Tobolla, a financial director at Citibank in Brazil; Italian Camillo Marina, a vice president of Generali do Brasil insurance company and Dutchman Louwerinus Hoogerheide, sales director of dairy company Parmalat Brasil.
The plane crashed shortly after take-off at 8:20 a.m. (1020 GMT), just two miles (3 km) from the airport.
"Parts of the plane fell on my roof and in my backyard. We heard a big crash and then windows and glass went flying all over the place," said housewife Eusa da Silva.
"We ran outside and all the neighbours were out screaming. Nobody knew what was going on," she said.
Nineteen year-old Rodrigo Carreiro said he drove to the scene of the disaster after dropping off a cousin and two friends at the airport, where they boarded the fatal flight.
"I begged them to stay because there was a party in Sao Paulo this evening. I can't believe this has happened.
"I left them and was leaving the airport when I heard there was an accident and that it was a TAM plane going to Rio. I came here immediately."

Chunks of fuselage, mortar and brick were strewn throughout a three block area where the plane came down. Hundreds of rescue workers formed human chains to remove rubble and aircraft remains in a search for injured residents.
Four residents were reportedly taken to a hospital but authorities said the injury list would probably be larger.

A TAM spokesman in Rio said the company was still investigating the cause of the crash. He said friends and relatives of the victims were gathering in a room provided by TAM where medical assistance and counselling was being offered.
"They are waiting for news of whether their relatives are on the flight or not," TAM's Jose Vivas Barreto said.
Some Rio-bound passengers who were scheduled to board flight 402 but were delayed by traffic in Sao Paulo breathed a big sigh of relief upon arriving in Rio via other flights.
"There was infernal traffic in Sao Paulo this morning and I missed the flight - Thank God!," said Luiz Paulo Rodriguez Relva, a construction workers.
Flights between Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro are common, leaving about every 30 minutes during the week. TAM has two morning flights from Sao Paulo to Rio Monday through Friday.
The airline was expected to hold a news conference later in the day to discuss the tragedy.
